scope_description: Shared evidence pack for Torggata → Youngstorget → Storgata / Brugata-Storgata. Research may be reused only where each claim's explicit place/entity scope permits it. Youngstorget is the active production target; Torggata is a reference/source anchor and must not be re-produced in this pilot.

claims.claim_text_or_structured_fact: Youngstorget is a named public square in central Oslo, bounded by Pløens gate, Eva Kolstads gate, Møllergata, Youngs gate and the Folketeater quarter; Torggata crosses the square.
claims.inference_limit: The boundary/crossing relation does not transfer Torggata's separate street history or businesses to Youngstorget.

claims.claim_text_or_structured_fact: The square was laid out/established in 1846.
claims.locator: S01 ingress; S02 ingress; S03 opening history
claims.inference_limit: Do not conflate the 1846 physical establishment with the 1852 official naming as Nytorvet.

claims.claim_text_or_structured_fact: The official name from 1852 through 1951 was Nytorvet.
claims.inference_limit: 1852 is a naming milestone, not evidence that the square itself was first established that year.

claims.claim_text_or_structured_fact: Youngstorget became the official name in 1951, after merchant Jørgen Young, who had owned the area where the square was laid out.
claims.inference_limit: The naming relation supports Jørgen Young's place connection; other biographical facts require People-owned evidence.

claims.claim_text_or_structured_fact: Youngstorget was intended as a market for agricultural products and for a long period was used especially as a cattle market; market activity became livelier after market traffic was moved there from Stortorvet in the 1850s.
claims.locator: S02 market-history paragraphs; S03 market-history section
claims.inference_limit: Do not describe the historical cattle-market function as the square's current primary use.

claims.claim_text_or_structured_fact: The Youngstorget bazaar structure dates from the 1870s and forms a persistent physical element of the square's market history.
claims.inference_limit: Object/building ownership must be resolved before materializing it as a Youngstorget Object or separate Place. Current tenants are not part of this claim.

claims.claim_text_or_structured_fact: The bronze full-figure sculpture Pioneren by Per Palle Storm was unveiled on Youngstorget in 1958.
claims.locator: S01 Kunst på Youngstorget; S03 Pioneren section
claims.inference_limit: Candidate for the Objects/kunst system; do not duplicate an existing canonical object/Place if one is found in phase 8.

claims.claim_text_or_structured_fact: A granite peace monument by sculptor Hagbart Solløs stands on Youngstorget and was erected in 1997 through LO and Nei til atomvåpen.
claims.inference_limit: Use the municipality's explicit facts only; do not infer additional commemoration chronology without a second source. Resolve canonical Object ownership before materialization.

claims.claim_text_or_structured_fact: Youngstorget has a permanent outdoor historical photo exhibition of 24 photographs, established in cooperation between Oslo municipality, LO and Arbeiderbevegelsens arkiv og bibliotek.
claims.inference_limit: The claim verifies the exhibition and partner organizations, not republication rights for its individual photographs.

claims.claim_text_or_structured_fact: Oslo municipality currently describes Youngstorget as used for demonstrations, commemorations/markings, market trade, outdoor serving, cultural events and other arrangements.
claims.inference_limit: This is a current municipal description, not evidence that every use occurs continuously or with equal frequency.

claims.claim_text_or_structured_fact: From 2023 Oslo municipality has worked on new rental guidelines and measures intended to improve the balance between everyday square life and large events on Youngstorget.
claims.inference_limit: Do not attribute social outcomes to the guidelines unless a source evaluates those outcomes.

claims.claim_text_or_structured_fact: The municipality lists completed Youngstorget measures including new seating, rehabilitated planters and planting, information displays, enhanced cleaning/safety measures, a permanent historical photo exhibition, new winter lighting and illuminated facade signs.
claims.inference_limit: Do not claim these measures caused improved safety, identity or usage unless an evaluation source supports that conclusion.

claims.claim_text_or_structured_fact: As of 2026-08-23, Oslo municipality lists fountain-light repair, stair lighting/signage, underground waste handling, outdoor-serving design guidelines and surface rehabilitation as planned measures for Youngstorget.
claims.inference_limit: Must remain explicitly qualified as planned; reverify before later publication because schedule/scope may change.

claims.claim_text_or_structured_fact: On 1 May 1890 a labour demonstration procession went from Youngstorget to Tullinløkka; Arbark's account states that roughly 4,000 workers took part.
claims.locator: S05 1 May 1890 section; S03 Youngstorget as assembly place
claims.inference_limit: Do not publish the stronger formulation 'the first May Day demonstration procession in the capital' as an unqualified strong claim until an independent second source is registered.

claims.claim_text_or_structured_fact: Youngstorget developed into a recurring assembly and demonstration place for the labour movement, with major mass gatherings particularly documented in the 1920s and 1930s.
claims.locator: S03 sections on samlingsplass and 1920s–1930s gatherings; S02 arbeiderbevegelsen
claims.inference_limit: Do not reduce the square's identity to only labour politics; market, everyday and other public uses are separately documented.

claims.claim_text_or_structured_fact: LO's 1 May 2026 Oslo programme used Youngstorget for the main Oslo gathering and speech before the procession.
claims.inference_limit: This verifies the 2026 event only; it does not prove future annual scheduling.

claims.claim_text_or_structured_fact: Oslo Museum's 2026 International Women's Day information directed participants to Youngstorget for the official Oslo programme beginning at 16:00 on 8 March 2026.
claims.inference_limit: This verifies the 2026 event only and should not be generalized into an undocumented continuous tradition.

claims.claim_text_or_structured_fact: Youngstorget underwent a major reworking in the mid-1990s; sources document a 1996 reopening/traffic change and installation of a newly cast copy of the historic fountain.
claims.locator: S02 1990s upgrade paragraph; S03 1996 ending section; S04 fountain/1996 captions
claims.inference_limit: Before/after asset pairing and exact traffic-design details require dedicated phase-7/19 source and rights review.

claims.claim_text_or_structured_fact: Oslo municipality's city-life analysis treats Youngstorget/Storgata as one planning sub-area and describes Torggata, Møllergata and Storgata as important connecting streets within that area.
claims.inference_limit: This shared planning context is not permission to copy specific facts, social histories or identities from one place to another.

claims.claim_text_or_structured_fact: TØI empirically studied interactions between cyclists and pedestrians in specified sections of Torggata and Brugata.
claims.inference_limit: Explicitly NOT scoped to `youngstorget`, `storgata` or `brugata_storgata_rusmiljo`. Geographic proximity and the word Brugata do not transfer this mobility evidence to those Places.

claims.claim_text_or_structured_fact: Storgata runs from Dronningens gate at Kirkeristen to Nybrua and is historically one of Oslo's old approach/traffic streets.
claims.inference_limit: Does not apply to Youngstorget or the Brugata/Storgata social-territory Place.

claims.claim_text_or_structured_fact: Storgata's present northern continuation to Nybrua was established as a continuous route when Nybrua was completed in 1827.
claims.inference_limit: Keep separate from Brugata's own earlier route history.

claims.claim_text_or_structured_fact: Brugata runs from Storgata to Vaterlands bru; before the 1827 Nybrua change it formed part of Vaterlands Storgade together with a western part of today's Storgata.
claims.inference_limit: No separate canonical `brugata` Place is created by this source pack. Do not attach this whole-street history to `brugata_storgata_rusmiljo`.

claims.claim_text_or_structured_fact: Brugata retains buildings rooted in 18th-century bondehandel, where agricultural traders could trade and stay outside the old city core.
claims.inference_limit: This is whole-street history, not evidence about Youngstorget or the contemporary open drug environment.

claims.claim_text_or_structured_fact: Oslo municipality has documented an open drug environment around the Brugata/Storgata intersection as a specific social territory; the canonical History GO Place is `brugata_storgata_rusmiljo`.
claims.locator: Municipal mapping sections already recorded in the canonical Place externalLinks
claims.inference_limit: Must not be generalized to all people or businesses in Brugata/Storgata, all of Storgata, all of Brugata, or Youngstorget. Reverify before downstream full production.

Resolve Object/kunst ownership and existing IDs before materialization.

conflicts_and_uncertainties.issue: Existing Youngstorget desc/popupDesc says the square was laid out as Nytorvet in 1852, conflating two different milestones.
Canonical place has year=1852, but repo policy does not define year universally as establishment year.
A separate canonical bare `brugata` Place was not established in Pilot 01 preflight.
conflicts_and_uncertainties.status: do_not_create_or_assume_place; keep evidence on entity street:brugata until canonical audit

held_back_claims.claim: The first May Day demonstration procession in the capital departed Youngstorget in 1890.
held_back_claims.reason: Strong 'first' claim currently supported by multiple Arbark pages from the same institution. Description contract requires at least two independent sources for disputed/strong claims before unqualified publication.
held_back_claims.next_research: Find and inspect an independent archival, museum, scholarly or reputable historical source.

held_back_claims.claim: The first women's demonstration procession departed Youngstorget in 1898.
held_back_claims.reason: Strong 'first' formulation located in Arbark material but not independently corroborated in this phase.
held_back_claims.next_research: Independent source required before publication as a strong claim.

held_back_claims.claim: 1956 was the first time the main May Day event was held on Youngstorget.
held_back_claims.reason: Arbark article and Arbark image series agree, but they are the same institution; independent corroboration is still required for the unqualified strong claim.
held_back_claims.next_research: Find independent newspaper/archive/LO or scholarly documentation.

held_back_claims.claim: Current brands/venues mapped to Youngstorget belong to the square because they are nearby.
held_back_claims.reason: Rejected by own-place gate. Address/proximity is insufficient; each Brand needs explicit place relation and canonical ownership audit.

held_back_claims.claim: TØI's Brugata mobility findings describe the canonical `brugata_storgata_rusmiljo` Place.
held_back_claims.reason: Rejected scope transfer. TØI studied pedestrian/cyclist interactions in Brugata street sections; the rusmiljø Place is a distinct social-territory object.
held_back_claims.next_research: Use the rusmiljø's own official social-geographic sources.

Research/resolve canonical Object IDs and ownership for Pioneren, Fredsmonumentet, fountain and bazaar before phase 8.
Perform full own-place People audit despite the existing >=22 mapping baseline; proximity to adjacent institutions is not enough.

Acquire before/after image pair(s) with inspectable provenance and publication rights; current historical image sources are research candidates, not automatically publishable assets.

Audit Lesespor items for direct Youngstorget relevance, accessibility and source quality.

torggata: No active new full production in Pilot 01. Existing Torggata source base remains the reference anchor.
Only genuinely shared source/claim material is reused; no Youngstorget production may trigger Torggata re-authoring.
storgata: Downstream production not started. Existing canonical record and verified geometry must be audited against current checklist before any new production.
Area-level Youngstorget/Storgata planning evidence is context only; build a Storgata-specific source pack extension when Storgata becomes active.
brugata_storgata_rusmiljo: Downstream production not started. Sensitive current social-geographic claims require freshness review before material revision.
Keep the social-territory Place distinct from whole-street Brugata and Storgata history and from mobility research.
street:brugata: Canonical bare Place ownership unresolved; do not create a new Place merely because the cluster name includes Brugata.
Historical street and TØI mobility evidence remains entity-scoped until the canonical audit resolves ownership.

freshness_notes: Historical claims with stable dates may be reused unless conflicting evidence appears.
Oslo municipality Youngstorget use/management/upgrades are institutional_periodic; planned measures are current_volatile and must remain qualified.
LO and Oslo Museum 2026 event claims are event-specific and must not be generalized into future schedules.
The Brugata/Storgata open-drug-environment source is sensitive and institutional_periodic; reverify when that Place becomes active.
TØI 2017 mobility observations are historical empirical data, not current traffic counts.

research_reuse_demonstrated_by: Torggata source base contributed already-reviewed TØI provenance without a new discovery pass.
Canonical rusmiljø externalLinks contributed official provenance without restamping it onto another Place.

One Youngstorget source pass now feeds description/history/object/current-use/before-after/quiz/related research surfaces through explicit claims instead of repeating source discovery for each surface.
reuse_measurement.note: Counts describe avoided duplicate work only. They are not a completion, richness or quality score.

phase_2_decision.blocking_rule: Any later surface that reaches an evidence gap must trigger additional Youngstorget-specific research rather than reduced content.
